current.faq_1_q: What is this tank made of?
current.faq_1_a: 80% premium Nylon, 20% Spandex. We tested dozens of fabric blends to find the exact ratio that gives you enough stretch and hold without feeling tight or suffocating. It's soft against the skin, breathes well, and holds its shape after repeated washing.
current.faq_2_q: Will the padding shift or fall out like other built-in bras?
current.faq_2_a: No. The padding stays in place while you wear it, it won't move around or bunch up. When you want to take it out, it comes out easily. Put it back in and it stays put, every single time.
current.faq_3_q: Will this work for my body type? I have a larger chest.
current.faq_3_a: The tank is designed to accommodate a wide range of body types and bust sizes. The distributed support structure means the hold comes from the entire garment, not just a narrow band - so there’s no single point bearing all the weight.
current.faq_4_q: Can I really wear this instead of a bra?
current.faq_4_a: That's exactly what it's designed for. Most of our customers wear it as their complete bra replacement for everyday activities: errands, school pickup, work, brunch, WFH, travel, lounging. It provides 'supported enough' comfort for daily life.
current.faq_5_q: Will this show through white or light-coloured clothing?
current.faq_5_a: The tank is designed with layering in mind. In neutral colours, it sits discreetly under light tops. For sheer or very thin white fabric, we recommend choosing a shade that’s close to your skin tone.
current.faq_6_a: Machine wash on a gentle cycle, cold water. Lay flat to dry or tumble dry on low. The fabric and padding are engineered to hold their shape and support through repeated washes. No special care required.

current.mt_why_heading: Here's Why Bras Stopped Working For You
current.mt_why_lead: It's not your body. It's the design.
current.mt_why_text: Traditional bras force all their support into three pressure zones: two straps and a band. That's it. Every gram of hold your body needs gets concentrated into those three narrow points.
current.mt_why_close: And because the support is concentrated, not distributed, those pressure points only get worse as the day goes on.
current.mt_list_heading: And Here's Why Nothing Else Has Worked Either
current.mt_list_1_text: Soft? Yes. Supportive? Barely. They feel lovely in the store, but under a real top, there's nothing there. No smoothing. No coverage.
current.mt_list_2_text: The elastic gives up after three washes. They roll up at the waist. The built-in 'bra' is a thin strip of fabric that flattens instead of supports.
current.mt_list_3_text: Designed for an hour at the gym, not twelve hours of living. Too tight. Too compressive. A nightmare to get on and off.
current.mt_list_4_text: Better than underwire, but they still use the same architecture: a band, two straps, and concentrated pressure.
current.mt_list_quote: The problem isn't that you haven't found the right bra.The problem is that you keep looking for the answer inside the same category that created the discomfort.

current.mt_ch_heading: What We Changed - And Why It Feels Different
current.mt_ch_sub: We didn't build a better bra. We stopped building bras entirely.
current.mt_ch_text: Instead of forcing support into two straps and a band, we spread it across the entire tank. No concentrated pressure points. No hardware. No architecture that digs, pinches, or rolls.
current.mt_ch_italic: This isn't shapewear. This isn't compression. This is "supported enough" - the feeling of being gently held and smoothly covered, without a single part of the tank fighting against your body.

current.mt_ch_1_text: The inner layer provides gentle, even hold across the entire torso. No narrow bands concentrating pressure.

current.mt_sf_bust_warn: This is not your bra size: measure around the fullest part of your bust, over your bra.
current.mt_sf_how: How do I measure my full bust?
current.mt_sf_how_steps:
1. Tape around you, across the fullest part of your bust.
  2. Keep it level all the way round your back.
  3. Snug, not tight: stand straight and breathe out normally.
  4. Read the inches (or cm) and type that number above.
